name: Burg Tratzberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Tratzberg between Jenbach and Stans is one of Europe's best-preserved Renaissance castles with original furnishings.
preis: Castle tour adults approx. €14.50; Tratzberg-Express train extra
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from early April to early November from 10:00 to 16:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The fairy-tale fortress Schloss Tratzberg rises majestically from a wooded ridge high above the Lower Inn Valley between Jenbach and Stans. First documented in the 13th century and rebuilt after a devastating fire around 1500 by the affluent Schwaz mining magnates Tänzel in late Gothic and early Renaissance style, Tratzberg ranks among the best-preserved authentic castles in all of Europe. It later came into the possession of the renowned Augsburg merchant family Fugger and eventually the Counts of Enzenberg, whose descendants lovingly inhabit the historic complex to this day. Visitors encounter not an empty shell, but a completely furnished palace featuring intricate timber ceilings, the famous Habsburg genealogical tree mural, precious armouries, and grand staterooms that bring Tyrolean aristocratic life vividly alive.

Route & Requirements

From the valley car park near Jenbach/Stans, an idyllic, shaded forest path ascends in about 20 minutes to the castle gate (approx. 100 vertical meters). Alternatively, guests can board the charming 'Tratzberg-Express' mini-train, which provides effortless and accessible transit right to the castle courtyard. Standard comfortable walking shoes and basic fitness are entirely sufficient for the walk. Interior tours are conducted via an innovative audio-drama guide with wireless headphones, tailored separately for adults and as an enchanting fairy-tale adventure for children. While the courtyard and restaurant are level, the guided tour includes historic staircases and uneven floorboards requiring steady footing. The courtyard offers wide views over the Inn Valley and Tux Alps.

Visit & Arrival

Schloss Tratzberg welcomes visitors daily from early April to early November between 10:00 and 16:00. Guided tour tickets and mini-train passes can be purchased at the valley ticket office or reserved online. By car, take the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Schwaz or Jenbach) and continue along the B171 to the signposted car park at Schlosswirt Tratzberg. Train passengers take the ÖBB to Jenbach station; from there, regional buses run nearby or visitors can follow the marked walking trail in roughly 30 minutes to the castle foot.

Tips

For visiting families, the children's audio-drama tour featuring castle ghost Tratzi and a hunt for hidden mice is an unforgettable highlight. Conclude your excursion with a meal at the traditional Schlosswirt tavern in the valley, enjoying hearty Tyrolean dishes in the shaded garden.
